{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Autonomy", "note": "The parent stepping in strips the kid of agency over their own standing on the team — they didn't choose this fight, but now they own it." },
  "read": "The kid is probably mortified and defensive at the same time — their parent just publicly questioned your judgment on their behalf, which makes them look like they can't earn their own spot. Their status in the team's eyes, and in yours, feels on the line through no action of their own.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Call the kid out, make clear the email changes nothing, maybe even hold them more accountable to prove a point — which signals you see them as the parent's puppet and poisons the relationship." },
  "mentorMove": "Separate the parent conversation from this kid completely — handle the email privately with the parent — then approach the player directly, quietly, and treat them like a capable athlete you genuinely respect, not a problem that just landed in your inbox.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "Your depth-chart decisions stay yours and are based on what you see in practice and games, full stop.",
    "The standard for earning a starting role does not shift because of outside pressure."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "You can give the player a clear, honest picture of exactly what they need to work on and a real timeline for reassessment.",
    "You can let them choose how they want to pursue those improvements — extra reps, film review, position-specific work — so they feel ownership."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, pull up for a sec. No big deal, just want to check in with you one-on-one real quick." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "How are you feeling about where things are at right now — with your role, with practice? I want to hear it straight from you, not from anyone else." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I see: you have got real ability, and there are two or three specific things that are keeping you from that starting spot right now. I want to lay those out for you plainly, and then I want you to tell me how you want to attack them — because that part is on you, and I think you can handle it." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I hold every player on this team to a high standard, and I am holding you to it because I genuinely believe you can get there. That does not change based on anything outside this building. What I need from you is to own this process yourself — and I am right here to help you do that." }
  ],
  "longGame": "If you keep this conversation clean — focused on the player's growth, not the parent's email — you build exactly the kind of trust that survives outside pressure. Over time the kid learns their standing on this team is something they earn themselves, and that you are a straight-shooter who sees them clearly. That is worth more than any starting spot."
}
situation: A player's parent emailed me arguing their kid should be starting, and the kid clearly knows about the email.
